newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call rises on back of new secured loans pact.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call rises on back of new secured loans pact.

text.p: Dutch call money rates rose one percentage point on Friday, pushed higher by the new secured loans pact which started running today and will end April 18.
Call money was bid between 2.75 and 2.81 percent, with most deals done at 2.75 percent dealers said. On Thursday, overnight money was changing hands at 1.75 percent.
The rise was considered quite normal given the new secured loans pact.

"Until yesterday, money market players could use what they had left from the old secured loans pact, which led to much liquidity. Now, they have to be more careful again, so call rates rose, as they were expected to," one dealer said.
Dealers said the allocation of the seven-day special advances pact which started today was not a factor behind the rise in call money rates.
Other money market rates barely moved and activity was focused on the short end, up to one month, dealers said.
They said call rates were likely to stick at the current level for a while if no new impulses moved the market.
"What we saw yesterday (call bid 1.50 to 1.81 percent) could not last. We have now reached a normal level," one dealer said.
